items.q: DKD develops in what share of diabetic patients?
items.exp: RISK: 50-60% of diabetic patients; ↑ with age. (Book p815)

items.q: The risk of DKD rises with age.
Match the following diabetes type to its screening timing — 1) Type 1 DM  2) Type 2 DM  3) The screening test … A) At diagnosis  B) Screen 5 yearly  C) Check for albuminuria
items.exp: T1 DM (type 1 diabetes mellitus) — screen 5 yearly; T2 DM — screen at diagnosis; screening = check for albuminuria. (Book p815)

items.q: The 'superior, but cumbersome' screening test is:
The routine screening test named is:
opts: Serum cystatin C at each visit

items.q: Match the following ACR level to its label — 1) <30 mg/g  2) 30-300 mg/g  3) >300 mg/g … A) Albuminuria  B) Normal  C) Microalbuminuria
items.exp: Levels: <30 normal; 30-300 microalbuminuria (endothelial injury): ↑ risk for thrombosis; >300 albuminuria. (Book p815)

items.q: The microalbuminuria band runs from 30 mg/g to:
Microalbuminuria marks endothelial injury with a raised thrombosis risk.
items.exp: Microalbuminuria (endothelial injury): ↑ risk for thrombosis. (Book p815)

items.q: A newly diagnosed type 2 diabetic patient is booked for DKD screening. When should the first check happen?
items.exp: T2 DM: screen at diagnosis. (Book p815)
